items.heading: Data Science Is a Real,
items.text: Data science is a real, growing field in India, not a hype bubble waiting to pop. But "is data science good" and "will I personally get a data science job easily" are two different questions, and most articles on this topic blur them together until you cannot tell which one is actually being answered.

items.heading: Here Is the Part Most
items.text: Here is the part most "data science scope in India" articles gloss over. The market-growth headline and an individual candidate's ease of getting hired next month are two different questions, and the gap between them is the actual source of "data science is oversaturated" panic.

items.heading: "Data Science" Gets Used As
items.text: "Data science" gets used as an umbrella term for three genuinely different jobs. Picking the wrong one under the same umbrella label is a common, expensive mistake that shows up only after the first year on the job. The order below leads with the lane that currently has the strongest pay ceiling and the most real growth headroom, ML/AI engineering, because it stacks software-engineering scale on top of ML skill, before the data-scientist and data-analyst lanes that follow.

items.heading: Most of That Growth Came
items.text: Most of that growth came from bootcamp graduates and career-switchers whose portfolios increasingly look identical: the same Titanic-dataset notebook, the same churn-prediction project copied from a tutorial.

items.heading: India Runs Hundreds of Data
items.text: India runs hundreds of data science and analytics certificate programs, most teaching the same narrow stack, basic Python, one ML library, one dashboard tool, with almost no differentiation between graduates.
